description: ODC: refactor an INHERITED MODEL -- maintenance work, not birth work. This job does NOT create the model: it inherits it from job:logic-steps (which inherits the data from job:data-full-model) and changes what was already there. The helper WfCov_Task_Describe, called from inside the foreach of the public action, is renamed WITH the real consumer linked; then it is duplicated (the copy is born without consumers, with the suffix the platform chooses), the consumer is re-pointed with replace, the old one is deleted without force and the original name returns to the copy. In between, the two inherited aggregate nodes and one inherited attribute are renamed, and the job READS BACK what followed and what was left behind: in the ODC lane the <Node>.<Output> expression is rewritten on its own (in the O11 lane the same expression keeps the old name and the module fails with ExpressionUnknownObject), while the consumer node name, the index name and the Description keep the old text and only a hand edit fixes them.

ops.name: WfCov_Task_Describe
ops._why: 1. THE STARTING POINT IS INHERITED: nothing here was created by this job. The helper, the public action that calls it and the entities come from job:logic-steps.
a REAL, inherited consumer: the Describe node inside the foreach EachOpen of WfCov_Project_CloseOpenTasks. It is this consumer that makes the rename and the replace interesting.
the BEFORE in writing: the expressions cite GetProject, GetOpenOfProject and WfCovTask.IsDone.

ops.name: WfLoadProject
ops._why: 2. RENAME AN INHERITED NODE, which is the <Node>.<Output> form of the question. Two inherited expressions read this node: the condition of the If (GetProject.List.Empty) and the final Assign (GetProject.List.Current.WfCovProject.Name). It returns consumers=3 and expressionsRewritten=2 -- in the rename of an AGGREGATE the ODC lane counts and rewrites the expressions that read the node output.

ops.name: WfLoadOpenTasks
ops._why: the same with four inherited readers: the RecordList of the foreach, the Assign of the loop, the argument of the helper call and the Summary.OpenTasks. It returns consumers=5 and expressionsRewritten=4.

READ BACK, THE CENTRAL PROOF: the SIX expressions already say WfLoadProject/WfLoadOpenTasks without a single manual fix -- WfLoadProject.List.Empty, WfLoadOpenTasks.List, WfLoadOpenTasks.Count and the three .List.Current. In the O11 lane this same dump would still show GetProject.List.Empty and Verify would give ExpressionUnknownObject: Can't identify 'GetProject' element in expression. Always compare by the dump, never only by the counter: it counts consumer objects, and there are cases (the action rename, further below) in which it returns 0 with the text correct all the same.

ops.name: IsClosed
ops._why: 3. RENAME AN INHERITED ATTRIBUTE (rename, not creation: so it follows the entity convention and does not carry the Wf prefix of new elements). It returns consumers=6 and expressionsRewritten=2: the two rewritten expressions are the aggregate filter and the loop Assign; the other four consumers are in the usages that follows.

who else held the inherited attribute, now with the new name: count=6 but real=3 -- the two rewritten expressions plus the EntityIndexAttribute of the index. The other three come with derived=true (the IRecordAttributeValue of the sample record and the two AttributeReference of the aggregates' attribute lists): these are things that Studio maintains on its own and that do not count as real use.

READ BACK WHAT DID NOT FOLLOW: the index Attributes followed (ProjectId, IsClosed) because they are references, but the index NAME still says ProjectDone, because a name is text. Only a hand edit fixes it -- and this job leaves it on purpose, so the difference is visible.
it is already WfCovTask.IsClosed in the aggregate filter and in the loop Assign.

ops.name: WfCov_Task_Caption
ops._why: 4. RENAME THE INHERITED ACTION WITH REAL CONSUMERS. The name was wrong: it returns a caption, not a description. It returns consumers=1 (the foreach node) and expressionsRewritten=0: here the zero is honest, because no inherited expression reads Describe.Title. Note the contrast with the aggregate rename above, which returned 2 and 4 -- the counter changes meaning with the type of the renamed object, so the proof is in the get that follows, not in the number.

READ BACK: the node's Action already points to WfCov_Task_Caption (link by key), but the node NAME is still Describe -- the node name only follows when it was equal to that of the action, and here it was the author who called it Describe.
5. DUPLICATE AN INHERITED ELEMENT. It is the Ctrl+D of Studio: the copy enters the same parent, at the end, and the suffix is chosen by the PLATFORM, not by the job.
the name the platform gave: WfCov_Task_Caption2. Note also Referrers=0 and that the copy brought the Description of the inherited original, word for word.
real=0: the copy is born WITHOUT consumers. It is not a defect, it is the meaning of the operation.
real=1: whoever used the original keeps using the original.

ops.value: Versao mantida da helper de legenda. Substituiu a WfCov_Task_Describe original.
ops._why: the copy is the one that will now be maintained; the Description is left on purpose citing the OLD name, so the end of the job shows that no rename touches it.
6. RE-POINT THE INHERITED CONSUMER. It is not find and replace of text: it is the same ReplaceReferences that Studio uses; the consumer node keeps the SAME key and only changes target.
the old one must stay at zero.
the inherited consumer is now here.
7. after the replace there are no consumers, so the delete passes WITHOUT force and brokenConsumers=0.

ops.name: WfCov_Task_Caption
ops._why: and only now is this name free: before the delete the rename would be refused for a collision in the same scope.
8. THE AFTER: the inherited node has the SAME key as the first usages above, and its Action now points to the key of the copy. It was the target that changed, not the consumer.

READ BACK WHAT DID NOT FOLLOW: the name is WfCov_Task_Caption again but the Key is the copy's, not that of the deleted original; and the Description still says WfCov_Task_Describe, a name that no longer exists in the module, because Description is author text.

ops.name: WfCov_Task_Describe
ops._why: empty list: the inherited name disappeared from the module, and the model is still valid.
the final state of the inherited public action: six expressions rewritten by the platform, one consumer re-pointed, zero manual fixes inside the flow.
